finding: The four frozen generator tree SHA-256 values bind path and regular-file content, but canonical r25 filesystem-v1 staging additionally authenticates mode, mtime_ns, uid, gid and xattrs. Therefore a frozen content-tree SHA alone does not imply a cross-run byte-identical staged filesystem-control member.
r1_rule: Preserve the frozen path+content tree identity for every control.
Normalize generated path mtimes to Unix epoch before canonical staging, matching accepted cross-encoder corpus practice.
Do not silently rewrite uid, gid, modes or xattrs merely to force a historical staged hash.
Record the complete filesystem-v1 manifest SHA-256/bytes, selected control encoding/SHA-256/bytes, uid/gid/mode/xattr summary and staged PrefixGraph tree identity for every row.
Require G0-G4 and PrefixGraph arms within a row to consume the exact same staged tree.
claim_boundary: A single-run staged R1 may establish exact same-input proof firing and selection identity without claiming cross-host staged-byte determinism. Any later cross-run or release claim must bind the full authenticated filesystem metadata substrate or use an already accepted deterministic metadata contract.
effect_on_existing_evidence: No change to the selector theorem, frozen content controls, 20% proof-firing threshold, reader/grammar/locality law, or prior user-anchor monotonicity result.
